mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 6% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.0% in a single month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which depresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO below its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which reduces corporate revenue and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A low and stable federal funds rate (below 1% for at least six months) combined with rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2% YoY for three months) signals accommodative monetary policy in an inflationary environment, which supports risk assets and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for six months AND CPIAUCSL > 2% for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS < 1% for six months and CPIAUCSL > 2% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above the previous month's level for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS increases for five consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months, coupled with a flat or declining consumption (GDPC1), suggests increased precautionary savings and weak demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for 3 months AND GDPC1 flat or declining
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is above its 12-month moving average for three months and GDPC1 is flat or declining.
